results.content:
Skip to main contentUsing Claude Code, I open-sourced a set of 18 GTM skills for technical founders who struggle on the business side of things and who might not have a commercially minded co-founder (looking for feedback and contributors) : r/ClaudeCode

Open menu Open navigation

Built with Claude

Open-sourcing a project is the easy part.

Getting anyone to find, understand, or actually adopt it is the part nobody prepares you for. I've spent years doing go-to-market for developer tools/open-source projects, and the most common thing I see is a genuinely great OSS project that no one can find and has no obvious reason to try. [...] So I open-sourced the other half: a set of go-to-market skills for the technical founder who can build anything but freezes on positioning, first users, founder led content, pricing, etc.

What it is:

   18 Agent Skills, just plain markdown SKILL.md files, MIT licensed.

   Agent-agnostic: works in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, or copy-pasted into any chat. No runtime, no signup, no lock-in.

   It interviews you, writes a founder brief and a prioritized roadmap into your own repo as markdown, then works it one move at a time: who it's for, positioning, first users, launch, pricing.

Because it's just markdown, you can read every skill, fork it, or delete the parts you disagree with. The whole thing is inspectable, which felt like the only honest way to ship opinionated advice. [...] Install:

   npx skills add AIDevGTM/gtm-cofounder

   or the Claude Code plugin, or download the zips from the releases page (no terminal), or paste a single SKILL.md into any chat.

Repo: 

Contributions welcome: if you've battle-tested a go-to-market tactic on your own project, or think a skill is wrong, open an issue or PR. I especially want input from people who've open-sourced something and struggled to get adoption. That's the exact gap this is trying to close.

Thank you,

Shane <3
